name: Dak Bungalow Curry
subtitle: the chicken curry cooked in colonial rest houses, thickened with a boiled egg and a potato

ingredients.note: fried before it goes in, which is what makes it a dak bungalow curry
pepper rather than chilli leads this curry

prepNotes: Dak bungalows were the rest houses on the mail routes. The khansama cooked whatever was to hand, which is why the dish carries a potato and an egg.
Fry the potato and the boiled eggs before they go in. That browning is the difference between this and an ordinary curry.

steps.text: Fry the halved potatoes in the oil until golden on all sides. Lift out. Fry the boiled eggs until blistered. Lift out.
In the same oil, brown the onion deeply with the bay leaves. Add the ginger and garlic and cook out.
Add the chicken, turmeric and half the pepper. Fry on high until sealed and coloured, 8 minutes.
Add 400ml water, cover and simmer 25 minutes. Return the potatoes for the last 15.
Add the eggs, the rest of the pepper, the garam masala and the vinegar. Simmer uncovered 5 minutes.
steps.tip: The vinegar goes in at the end. Boiled long it just tastes sour.

steps.text: Rest 10 minutes before serving with bread or rice.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and is better on day two. Take the eggs out before freezing; boiled whites go rubbery.
